One country on this map has a homicide rate over 50x higher than neighbors just across the border.

The world's murder rate, mapped — a thread 🧵🗺️

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
1/ The darkest reds cluster in one place: Latin America. Mexico, Honduras, Colombia and Venezuela all sit above 20 homicides per 100,000 people — some of the worst-hit spots run past 50.
2/ Compare that to Western Europe and East Asia, mostly under 1 per 100,000. Japan and Switzerland are safer, by this measure, than almost anywhere on Earth.

3/ Why the gap? Researchers point to weak state institutions, drug-trafficking routes through Central America and Mexico, and gangs filling power vacuums left by fragile governments — not poverty alone, since plenty of poor countries stay low on this map.

4/ Southern Africa is the map's other hotspot: South Africa sits near the top globally, a pattern criminologists trace partly to apartheid-era inequality and policing gaps that were never fully repaired.
5/ The US stands out among wealthy nations: still several times higher than Canada or Western Europe, though far below Latin America's worst rates — and roughly half what it was in the early 1990s.

6/ Borders on a war map show where violence happened. This one shows where it's still happening, every year.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
